text:
Euro-Dollar Exchange Rates To Face German Inflation, FED And US Jobs This Week Euro-Dollar Exchange Rates To Face German Inflation, FED And US Jobs This Week Facebook The Week Ahead on the Foreign Exchange Markets: The Fed Meeting and NFP Highlights of a Busy Week for the Dollar and the Euro Exchange Rates
Data will be watched especially closely in the coming weeks and months as central banks such as the Fed, the ECB and the BoE are all assessing data to help shape their next move.
This week see significant releases such as German inflation, the Fed meeting on Wednesday and the all important US jobs report on Friday.
The US dollar broke out of a persist range and could extend higher if data or the Fed support a hawkish view. The DXY is now nearly flat for the year.
This week has some important releases and events likely to cause volatility in many markets. The Fed meeting and Friday’s US jobs report will affect currencies, and stocks will see some wild moves as earnings season reaches a peak.
Last week saw some interesting moves in many currencies with GBP especially weak as soft data put a rate hike in May in doubt. The Euro was also weak after the ECB continued to stall and traders were left guessing their next move. The USD continued higher, obviously on the back of weakness elsewhere, but also helped on by domestic yields. With the 10 year breaking 3%, the dollar looked to be driven by rate differentials once more after ignoring them for much of the year.
The main takeaway from last week was just how data will be for central bank policy going forward. The ECB is clearly taking a data dependent “wait and see” stance, and the Bank of England may have to put off plans for its next hike due to a dip in UK inflation and GDP. So with this in mind, here are this week’s important releases.
Monday April 30
There are quite a few market closures today, China takes Labor Day early, and Japan, India and Hungary are closed for local holidays, so expect a quiet Asian session. The important news of the day is the German inflation print.
Tuesday May 1
China takes an additional Labor Day today, along with most of Europe (but not the UK). Trump’s infamous steel and aluminum tariffs come into force, except for exempted countries (Canada, EU and Australia are exempt). If NAFTA is not concluded by then (a strong likelihood), the Canada (and Mexico) exemptions are expected to continue. No surprises are expected from RBA Governor Lowe or BoC Governor Poloz, although Canadian GDP may cause a ripple. Otherwise the big news of the day is the AAPL earnings after the bell.
Wednesday May 2
Wednesday is FOMC rate decision day, with a 93.3% expectation (per CME FedWatch) of a hold. Attention will therefore turn to the dot-plot and Chair Powell’s remarks. Expect USD positioning throughout the day. The ADP estimate is 200k, almost exactly the same as the NFP estimate of 198k. There are no other Fed speakers today, only hawkish Bundesbank President Weidmann.
Thursday May 3
Thursday is the hiatus between FOMC and NFP so some volatility many ensue. ECB speakers are Hansson (07:00), Constancio (12:00) and Coeuré (13:30), although the speech by SNB President Jordan at 16:00 may be interesting now that EURCHF has finally recovered to its pre-Jan 2015 level. Poland and Japan are closed today.
Friday May 4
NFP is always important, but as always recently, the Average Hourly Earnings is the key to a June rate hike (or not). The YoY estimate of 2.7% is the same as last month’s actual print, whereas the MoM estimate is down to 0.2% (0.3% prev act). Any miss here could stall the dollar’s recent rally. CB speakers today: Dudley (hawkish, voter) at 16:00, Williams (hawkish, voter) at 19:00, Quarles (centrist, voter) at 21:30, and ECB (BuBa) Weidmann at 13:00. Japan is closed again today.
